addresses.name: CAIUnit::BuildAirTargetProvinceLists
addresses.comment:
**The writer of all four `air_target_provinces_*` lists** (`CAIUnit +0x1FC`, `+0x20C`, `+0x21C`, `+0x22C`). 0x4B4740 to the `ret 4` at 0x4B4E59. One caller: CAIUnit::Tick at 0x4B0A4F, under `agent->unit != 0` and then `fullPass || !air_target_lists_built (+0x83)` - fullPass being the tick's own flag, hour == (id+6) % 24 or full_pass_pending (+0x84) - **so the lists are rebuilt at every daily full pass**, and also the first time an agent ticks with a unit.

**Step 1, the candidate set.** `CAIUnit::GetArea(agent)` (0x4BBAE0); with none, the theatre of the agent's unit's province (`CMapProvince +0x380`/`+0x384`) through FindPersistentById. All four lists emptied (CListOfOwned_ClearByPointer x4). Candidates are the **AirBases** (`CCountry +0xD70`, the Lua's GetAirBases) of our own country, of our **Overlord** (`+0xF38`/`+0xF3C`) when we are a subject (`isSubject +0xF34`), and of every one of our **Vassals** (`+0xF78`), each kept when its theatre id (`+0x380`/`+0x384`) is the area's; the test on the province's base object (`+0x54`, a CUnitBaseProvince) slot 1 is IsCarrier, false for every province base, so it never refuses. Separately, a vector of the AirBases of every country in `enemies (+0x1008)` that is in the scenario (`+0x44`) lying in that country's acting capital's area.

**Step 2, four scores per candidate, one appended to each list.** Each is a 0x10-byte CPersistent record - vftable 0x15EB644, save id 0x18D at `+4`, the province id at `+8` and the float at `+0xC` - inserted by CList_InsertByAscendingScore (0x4DD590), lowest first.

| list | appended at | scored against (CAIUnit::MeanDistanceToProvinceList) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `+0x1FC` default | 0x4B4C68 | the ops area (`+0x90`) when `frontier_at_war (+0x364)` is set, else the enemy air-base vector; blended `0.75 * s(invasion_target_provinces +0x1AC) + 0.25 * s(that)` when `+0x1AC` is non-empty |
| `+0x20C` strategic | 0x4B4CC1 | `strategic_target_provinces (+0x18C)`, which CEU3AI_AssignSeaTargetsToAgents fills with enemy war-industry provinces |
| `+0x21C` naval | 0x4B4D1A | `enemy_sighting_provinces (+0x19C)`, the provinces of the enemy fleets assigned to the agent (+0x25C) |
| `+0x22C` transport | 0x4B4E00 | `invasion_target_provinces (+0x1AC)`, and only while the vector +0x16C is non-empty (the gate at 0x4B4D1F, the reader's gate inverted) |

It finishes by setting `agent->+0x83 = 1` (0x4B4E18) and freeing both temporaries.

**Why no earlier pass found it:** it reaches every list through a plain `lea reg, [agent + 0x1FC]`; the scan that missed it was limited to recorded function entries.

**Only the country's own air bases are held to the area** (`FINDINGS-liveread.md`, section 27): the theatre-id test at 0x8B4849 sits in the first loop alone; the overlord's (0x8B48E7) and the vassals' (0x8B4989) air bases are appended wherever they lie. Read from memory on the save of July 1941: the United Kingdom's Home and Far East lists both carry Singapore (Iraq's) and an Omani base, and Oman's carries every British air base in the world.

addresses.name: CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits
addresses.comment:
**The theatre agent's air groups, every hour it holds one.** Body 0x4CD890-0x4D051D (trap 3: the `ret 8` at 0x4CEE68 is a shared epilogue mid-function). Gate: air_units_count (+0x104) >= 1. Four phases (FINDINGS-reorganise.md, FINDINGS-airnaval4.md): (1) 0x4CDA90 triage of +0xFC (kept by InsertUnitByRange, shortest range first, equals in slot 78's walk order): a dead join_air cancelled; at war, a group whose base province has enemy land units marching in is pulled out of any order but rebase_air and **sets force**; fitness bars 0.5/0.75 at air stance 2, else 0.7/0.85, halved for a CAG or interceptor group; an unfit busy group gets carrier_protection (all CAG, on a carrier) or none; a tired idle group at its base rests. (2) 0x4CE1E9 rebase, only with force: the list is +0x20C (strategic bomber or strategic_attack > 50000), +0x21C (naval bomber), +0x22C (transport plane, and the group is skipped while +0x16C is non-empty) or +0x1FC; the running best starts at the current base province with score 1e6, so the lowest listed base below 1e6 wins and the current one is not scored; a province with enemy land units marching in is skipped; score = the list's float, made (score + DistanceBetweenProvinces(the agent's HQ province, it)) x 0.5 when the group's parent is not at oob level 0; without a transport plane, x load where load = (this pass's arrivals + wings based there + the group's own unless based there) / the air base's level_current, when above 1.0; strict lower wins, first of equals in list (ascending) order; a winner other than the current base gets rebase_air and the arrivals tally moves. (3) 0x4CE64F split and merge. The hinge 0x4CEDA8: a regroup this pass (+0x88) with runs_units or allow_hq_reorg returns 1 with no missions; otherwise missions need force or war and air stance != 0. (4) 0x4CEE76 missions; **the anti-shipping budget is 4 x threatened_provinces_count (+0x1E4)** - the provinces of ours an enemy force at sea is heading for - so a tactical or CAS wing with sea attack flies naval missions only while such a threat stands. The returned bool is not read. The second argument is an int whose byte 3 is read uninitialised and ignored.

**The rebase's crowding, read again 2026-11-10** (`FINDINGS-liveread.md`, section 26): the wings based at a candidate are the regiments of every air unit on the list of the province's air base object (`CMapProvince +0x54`, its list at +4), nested under a headquarters or not, and the group's own are added unless that air base object is the group's (`CUnit +0x98`). On the save of July 1941 Brazil's three bases all score 10000 on every list, and the crowding alone keeps its groups where they are. The CAG test at 0x8CE240 skips a group with any carrier wing before anything else; a group whose own base is not on the list keeps that base when nothing scores under 1e6.

**The triage's four thresholds are two pairs, each used for strength and organisation alike** (`FINDINGS-liveread.md`, section 27): at plan air stance 2 a wing under 0.5 of either is unfit (`[ebp-28]`, `[ebp-3C]` from the float at 0x14BB304 in the running image) and one under 0.75 of either damaged or tired (`[ebp-80]`, `[ebp-A4]`); otherwise 0.7 and 0.85; all halved for a carrier's or an interceptor group. An unfit group under a busy order is called off; a group with any wing damaged or tired, idle at its own base, rests - that is the higher pair, not the unfit one.
